version.description: The configuration contract version. Optional for a single-owner file so that files written before it existed keep loading; required as soon as `owners` is used, because that shape has never existed without it.

owner.description: A GitHub login: an organisation or a personal account. octoform tells which one it is by asking the API, not by anything declared here — an organisation and a user with the same login are indistinguishable in configuration, and forcing the author to say which invites the file to be wrong about it.

owners.description: Accounts to govern, keyed by GitHub login. Each entry may narrow or override what the root declares for all of them.

imports.description: Other configuration files to merge before this one, most general first. Paths are resolved relative to the file that lists them, so an imported file can itself import further files. This is how a set of type presets is shared across several owners without copying it around: put `types` and `defaults` in a file with no `owner` of its own, and import it from each real configuration.

policies.description: Reusable policy fragments, keyed by a name of the author's choosing, that any layer folds in through its own `policies` list. A policy may reference other policies; a reference cycle is reported with the full chain.

repos.description: Per-repository overrides. Only valid in a single-owner file: a bare repository name identifies nothing on its own once more than one account is in scope, so a multi-owner file declares these under their owner.

Config.description:
A configuration file as it is written, before normalization.

Two shapes are accepted. A single-owner file names its account in `owner` and declares policy at the root; a multi-owner file lists accounts under `owners` and keeps the root for what they share. Declaring both is an error: the two cannot be reconciled without deciding, on the author's behalf, which account the root-level policy was meant for.

ConfigVersion.description:
The configuration contract a file is written against.

It is not the version of octoform. It changes only when the meaning of an existing key changes, which is what lets a future release read an old file correctly instead of guessing.

OwnerBlock.description: Everything one GitHub owner can declare under `owners`.

property.description: Name of the GitHub custom property holding the type.

ClassifyConfig.description: Classification rules and optional organization property storage.

json.description: Shallow key/value match against the JSON file named by `file_exists`.

ClassifyRule.description: A condition used to infer a repository's type when it has none recorded.

AuditConfig.description: Audit-only expectations. These never mutate anything; they exist so that "every public repository must have a description" is a line of configuration rather than a branch in the code.

policies.description:
Named entries of the root `policies` block to fold in before this layer's own keys, in declaration order.

A policy is a reusable fragment of ordinary policy, nothing more: it has no meaning of its own and cannot express anything a layer could not express inline. Referencing one never overrides a key the referencing layer states itself, so reading a layer top to bottom still tells the whole story.

manage.description: When false, the repository is still inventoried and audited but no policy is applied to it. Distinct from `exclude`, which drops it entirely.

PolicySet.description: Everything that can be declared at any level of the precedence chain.

sponsorships.description: Whether the repository shows a sponsor button.

pull_requests.description: Whether pull requests can be opened at all. Turning this off does not remove the ones that already exist.

FeaturePolicy.description: Desired state for repository feature switches.

MergePolicy.description:
Desired state for pull-request merge behavior.

Each message default is named after the `allow_` switch it belongs to, since squash merges and merge commits carry their own independent pair. GitHub refuses a request that sets a message default without also stating the matching title, so declaring one without the other is reported rather than sent — see `planScalars`.

SquashCommitTitle.description:
Where the title of a squash merge commit comes from by default.

`PR_TITLE` always uses the pull request's title; `COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE` uses the single commit's title when there is exactly one, and the pull request's title otherwise.

SquashCommitMessage.description: Where the body of a squash merge commit comes from by default.

MergeCommitTitle.description: Where the title of a merge commit comes from by default. `MERGE_MESSAGE` is GitHub's own "Merge pull request #123 from branch" wording.

MergeCommitMessage.description: Where the body of a merge commit comes from by default.

immutable_releases.description: Whether published releases and their assets become immutable. An owner can enforce this across its repositories, in which case a repository cannot turn it off and octoform reports that instead of attempting it.

SecurityPolicy.description: Desired state for repository security features.

archived.description: Whether the repository is archived. Archiving is reversible, but while it lasts GitHub refuses every write, so it is applied after everything else and only when everything else succeeded.

template.description: Whether the repository can be used as a template for new ones.

name.description:
Desired name of the repository, renamed only from one of  {@link  RepoPolicy.rename_from } .

Repositories are declared under `repos.<name>`, so a rename outlives the entry that asked for it: once it happens, that entry no longer matches anything. The plan says so before it happens rather than leaving it to be discovered on the next run.

rename_from.description: Rename to `name` only when the repository currently has one of these.

RepoPolicy.description: Desired state for repository metadata and access settings.

CreationPolicy.description:
Who may open an issue or a pull request on the repository.

`COLLABORATORS_ONLY` still leaves the feature enabled and its history readable; it narrows who can add to it. Turning the feature off entirely is a different setting.

RepositoryVisibility.description:
A visibility a repository can be set to.

`internal` is deliberately absent. GitHub reports it on a repository but its update endpoint does not accept it, so octoform can observe an internal repository and never restore one — a policy that could name it would be offering a door that only opens one way.

name.description: Desired name of the default branch.

rename_from.description: Rename the default branch to `name` only when it currently has one of these.

DefaultBranchPolicy.description: Desired default-branch name and guarded rename sources.

enforce_admins.description: Apply every rule here to administrators too.

require_pull_request.description: Require a pull request. The review keys below configure it and imply it.

bypass_pull_request_allowances.description: Who may merge without the required reviews.

restrict_pushes.description: Who may push at all. Organisation repositories only.

lock_branch.description: Make the branch read-only, for everyone.

BranchProtectionPolicy.description: Classic branch protection for one branch, named.

BranchRestrictions.description:
Who a branch-protection restriction names.

Users are logins, teams are slugs and apps are slugs — GitHub's protection endpoint takes them by name rather than by id, unlike its ruleset bypass actors, so nothing here has to be resolved before it can be sent.

require_pull_request.description: Require a pull request. The keys below configure it and imply it.

checks_not_enforced_on_create.description: Let a branch be created without the required checks having run.

allow_fetch_and_merge.description: Allow an otherwise blocked update when it is a fetch and merge.

workflows_not_enforced_on_create.description: Let a branch be created without the required workflows having run.

target_branches.description: Branch names or patterns, including `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` and `~ALL`.

target_pushes.description: A push ruleset, which governs the whole repository and matches no refs.

exclude.description: Refs matching any of these are exempt, whatever the target matched.

bypass.description: Who may bypass these rules. Omitting this keeps whoever GitHub already lets past; an empty list is what removes them.

RulesetPolicy.description:
A desired ruleset.

Exactly one of the three target keys says what the ruleset governs, and the key names which. A single `target` field plus a shared list of patterns would let a file say `target: tag` beside `target_branches`, which is a disagreement nothing could resolve.

MergeQueueRule.description: Desired merge queue behaviour, when a ruleset requires one.

CodeScanningRule.description: How much of a code scanning tool's output blocks a merge.

negate.description: Match everything the pattern does not, instead of what it does.

name.description: Shown by GitHub when the rule rejects a push.

PatternRule.description: A rule matching some piece of commit or ref text against a pattern.

PatternOperator.description: How a pattern rule compares the text it is given.

path.description: Path to the workflow file from the root of its repository.

repository.description: `owner/name` of the repository holding it. Defaults to this repository.

repository_id.description: The id of  {@link  WorkflowRequirement.repository } , resolved or written.

ref.description: Branch or tag to take the file from.

sha.description: Commit to take the file from.

WorkflowRequirement.description:
A workflow that has to pass before a change reaches a targeted ref.

GitHub identifies the workflow's repository by numeric id, not by name, so `repository` is resolved before the rule can be sent, and `repository_id` is the form the rule comes back in. A policy normally writes the name; writing the number instead is allowed and skips the lookup, which is the only way to name a repository the token cannot read.

RulesetEnforcement.description: How strictly a ruleset is applied. `evaluate` reports what would have been blocked without blocking it, and GitHub offers it only on some plans.

deploy_keys.description: Every deploy key on the repository, which GitHub grants as one actor.

RulesetBypass.description:
Actors that may bypass a ruleset, grouped by the mode they bypass in.

Grouping by mode rather than listing each actor with its own is what keeps the common case — one exception, granted to several people at once — from repeating the mode on every line. A policy that needs two modes writes two groups.

Everything here is named except `roles`. GitHub's ruleset endpoints take a repository role as a numeric id, and its REST surface has no route that maps a repository-role name to one: only *organisation* roles can be listed. So the number is what a policy writes, rather than a name octoform would have to translate through a table it cannot verify.

BypassMode.description:
When an actor may bypass a ruleset.

`pull_request` only lets the actor past on a pull request, and GitHub accepts it on branch rulesets only. `exempt` skips the rules entirely and writes no bypass entry to the audit log, so it is the one mode that leaves no trace of having been used.

reviewers.description: GitHub logins that must approve a deployment to this environment.

EnvironmentPolicy.description: Desired deployment environment and its user reviewers.

from.description: Path to the local file to copy, relative to the configuration file.

FileMode.description: Supported behavior when reconciling a declared repository file.

policies.description:
Named entries of the root `policies` block to fold in before this layer's own keys, in declaration order.

A policy is a reusable fragment of ordinary policy, nothing more: it has no meaning of its own and cannot express anything a layer could not express inline. Referencing one never overrides a key the referencing layer states itself, so reading a layer top to bottom still tells the whole story.

manage.description: When false, the repository is still inventoried and audited but no policy is applied to it. Distinct from `exclude`, which drops it entirely.

RepoEntry.description: A repository entry: a policy layer plus the type it is classified as.

ExcludeConfig.description: Repositories dropped from every command, by name.
